label: Bilateral shoulder — prior dislocation, rotator-cuff/labrum; LIMITED external-rotation ROM (no pain)
description: Both shoulders, history of dislocation with rotator-cuff/labral involvement. Manifests as LIMITED external-rotation range of motion (presses fine, but the arms can't travel further back than ~neutral). No pain. Notably: sedentary -> symptoms worsen; consistent upper-body training -> symptoms resolve, so upper-body volume is THERAPEUTIC.
red_flags: a sense of the shoulder slipping / instability
numbness or tingling down the arm
intake_questions: Which positions feel like the shoulder might slip?
Painless ROM limit or any pain?
Worse when sedentary, better when training?
workaround: Train WITHIN available ROM: do NOT force external rotation / horizontal abduction past neutral. AVOID behind-the-neck press or pulldown, wide-grip end-range stretch positions, deep dips, and ballistic/jerky overhead. FAVOR neutral-grip and front-of-body pressing (he presses fine), controlled tempo, full-but-pain-free ROM. EMPHASIZE rotator-cuff + scapular-stability work and generous upper-body volume — it is therapeutic for him and protects the labrum. The apprehension position (abduction + end-range external rotation) is the single thing to avoid.
notes: Bilateral. Upper-body training is therapeutic -> program generous upper volume within ROM. Not a broad pressing/pulling gate; it's a ROM/technique modification + a cuff/scapular emphasis.
